title: Simple past — regular verbs
context:
# Simple Past (Pretérito Perfeito Simples) — Regular Verbs

The **Pretérito Perfeito Simples (PPS)** is the most common past tense in Portuguese. It is used to describe completed actions that took place at a specific point in the past.

### Regular Verb Endings
For regular verbs, remove the infinitive ending (**-ar**, **-er**, **-ir**) and add the PPS endings:

| Pronoun | -ar (*falar*) | -er (*comer*) | -ir (*partir*) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **eu** | fale**i** | com**i** | part**i** |
| **tu** | fal**aste** | com**este** | part**iste** |
| **ele/ela/você** | fal**ou** | com**eu** | part**iu** |
| **nós** | fal**ámos** | com**emos** | part**imos** |
| **eles/elas/vocês** | fal**aram** | com**eram** | part**iram** |

*Note: In European Portuguese, the **nós** form of **-ar** verbs takes an acute accent (**falámos**, **comprámos**) to distinguish it from the present tense (*falamos*).*

### Common Past Time Expressions
- **ontem** — yesterday
- **anteontem** — the day before yesterday
- **ontem à noite** — last night
- **na semana passada** — last week
- **no mês passado** / **no ano passado** — last month / last year
- **há dois dias** / **há um ano** — two days ago / a year ago

**Watch out!**
1. Third-person singular endings are distinct: **-ou** for *-ar* (*Ele falou*), **-eu** for *-er* (*Ele comeu*), and **-iu** for *-ir* (*Ele partiu*).
2. Third-person plural endings end in **-am** (*falaram*, *comeram*, *partiram*).

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: «Comprei» is the 1st-person PPS form of the regular -ar verb «comprar»: «eu comprei» (I bought).
exercises.sentence: Yesterday I **bought** a new book in Lisbon.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: «Ontem» means yesterday and is the most common past time marker.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: «Comeu» is the 3rd-person PPS form of the regular -er verb «comer»: «ele comeu» (he ate).

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: «Abri» is the 1st-person PPS form of the regular -ir verb «abrir»: «eu abri» (I opened).
exercises.sentence: I **opened** the window in the morning.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: «Escreveu» is the 3rd-person PPS form of the regular -er verb «escrever»: «ela escreveu» (she wrote).
exercises.sentence: Maria **wrote** a long letter to her grandmother.

exercises.prompt: Fill the gaps: "Yesterday I spoke with Pedro and bought bread."
exercises.explanation: 1st-person PPS for -ar verbs ends in -ei: «falei» and «comprei».
exercises.template: Ontem eu ___ com o Pedro e ___ pão.

exercises.prompt: Fill the gaps: "Last week Tiago worked a lot and wrote a report."
exercises.explanation: 3rd-person singular PPS: -ar verbs end in -ou («trabalhou»), -er verbs in -eu («escreveu»).
exercises.template: Na semana passada o Tiago ___ muito e ___ um relatório.

exercises.prompt: Fill the gaps: "Did you drink water and eat the soup yesterday?" (informal)
exercises.explanation: 2nd-person (tu) PPS: -er verbs end in -este: «bebeste» and «comeste».
exercises.template: Tu ___ água e ___ a sopa ontem?

exercises.prompt: Fill the gaps: "The train left at eight and the museum opened at nine."
exercises.explanation: 3rd-person PPS of regular -ir verbs ends in -iu: «partiu» and «abriu».
exercises.template: O comboio ___ às oito e o museu ___ às nove.

exercises.prompt: Fill the gaps: "Yesterday evening we dined late and drank tea."
exercises.explanation: Past time marker «ontem à noite»; «nós jantámos» (-ar) and «bebemos» (-er).
exercises.template: Ontem à noite nós ___ tarde e ___ chá.

exercises.prompt: Fill the gaps: "Last year the students learned Portuguese and wrote poems."
exercises.explanation: 3rd-person plural PPS of -er verbs ends in -eram: «aprenderam» and «escreveram».
exercises.template: No ano passado os alunos ___ português e ___ poemas.

exercises.prompt: Fill the gaps: "Two days ago I decided to visit the castle and bought a ticket."
exercises.explanation: «Há dois dias» (two days ago); 1st-person PPS: «decidi» (-ir) and «comprei» (-ar).
exercises.template: ___ dois dias eu ___ visitar o castelo e ___ um bilhete.

exercises.prompt: State a past action: "Yesterday I spoke with the teacher."
exercises.explanation: The «eu» form of -ar verbs in the PPS ends in -ei: «falar» → «falei».
acceptedAnswers: Eu ontem falei com o professor.

exercises.prompt: State eating in the past: "Tiago ate a warm soup."
exercises.explanation: The 3rd-person singular PPS of -er verbs ends in -eu: «comer» → «comeu».
acceptedAnswers: Tiago comeu uma sopa quente.

exercises.prompt: State a departure: "The train to Porto left at ten o'clock."
exercises.explanation: The 3rd-person singular PPS of -ir verbs ends in -iu: «partir» → «partiu».
acceptedAnswers: O comboio para o Porto partiu às dez.

exercises.prompt: State past residence: "Last year we lived in an apartment in Braga."
exercises.explanation: The «nós» form of -er verbs in the PPS ends in -emos: «vivemos» (same as the present; «no ano passado» shows it is past).
acceptedAnswers: Nós no ano passado vivemos num apartamento em Braga.

exercises.prompt: State buying something: "Ana bought a warm jacket at the shopping centre."
exercises.explanation: The 3rd-person singular PPS of -ar verbs ends in -ou: «comprou». In Portugal a mall is «o centro comercial».
acceptedAnswers: Ana comprou um casaco quente no centro comercial.

exercises.prompt: Describe a past visit: "Last week they visited the castle and the museum."
exercises.explanation: The 3rd-person plural PPS of -ar verbs ends in -aram: «visitar» → «visitaram».
acceptedAnswers: Na semana passada visitaram o castelo e o museu.

exercises.prompt: State working late: "Yesterday I worked until eight at the office."
exercises.explanation: The «eu» form of -ar verbs ends in -ei: «trabalhei». «Até às oito» = until eight.
acceptedAnswers: Eu ontem trabalhei até às oito no escritório.

exercises.prompt: State learning something: "The students learned many new words in class yesterday."
exercises.explanation: The 3rd-person plural PPS of -er verbs ends in -eram: «aprender» → «aprenderam».
acceptedAnswers: Os alunos aprenderam muitas palavras novas na aula ontem.

exercises.prompt: Describe a past decision: "Two days ago Rita decided to change apartments."
exercises.explanation: «Há dois dias» = two days ago; the 3rd-person singular PPS of -ir verbs ends in -iu: «decidiu».
acceptedAnswers: Há dois dias Rita decidiu mudar de apartamento.

exercises.prompt: State writing a message: "Last night I wrote an email to reception."
exercises.explanation: The «eu» form of -er verbs in the PPS ends in -i: «escrever» → «escrevi».
acceptedAnswers: Ontem à noite eu escrevi um email à receção.

exercises.prompt: State running in the morning: "Before breakfast Pedro ran five kilometres."
exercises.explanation: The 3rd-person singular PPS of -er verbs ends in -eu: «correr» → «correu».
acceptedAnswers: Antes do pequeno-almoço Pedro correu cinco quilómetros.

exercises.prompt: Pedro answers: «Comprei um casaco novo.» Ask him (informal) what he bought.
exercises.explanation: «O que compraste?» uses the 2nd-person (tu) PPS form of comprar.
acceptedAnswers: O que é que compraste?

exercises.prompt: Sofia answers: «Comi peixe com batatas.» Ask her (informal) what she ate.
exercises.explanation: «O que comeste?» uses the tu form of the PPS of -er verbs, ending in -este.
acceptedAnswers: O que é que comeste?

exercises.prompt: Tiago answers: «Ontem à noite.» Ask him (informal) when he arrived in Lisbon.
exercises.explanation: «Quando…?» asks when; the tu PPS of -ar verbs ends in -aste: «chegaste». Arriving in a city is «chegar a».
acceptedAnswers: Quando é que chegaste a Lisboa?

exercises.prompt: Ana answers: «Abri a loja às nove horas.» Ask her (informal) what time she opened the shop.
exercises.explanation: «A que horas…?» asks the clock time; the tu PPS of -ir verbs ends in -iste: «abriste».
exercises.givenAnswer: Abri a loja às nove horas.
acceptedAnswers: A que horas é que abriste a loja?

exercises.prompt: Your colleague answers: «Trabalhei oito horas ontem.» Ask him (informal) how many hours he worked yesterday.
exercises.explanation: «Hora» is feminine, so «Quantas horas…?»; the tu PPS of -ar verbs ends in -aste: «trabalhaste».
acceptedAnswers: Quantas horas é que trabalhaste ontem?
Ontem, quantas horas trabalhaste?

exercises.prompt: Your friends answer: «Sim, visitámos o museu de arte ontem.» Ask them (vocês) whether they visited the museum yesterday.
exercises.explanation: «Vocês» takes the 3rd-person plural PPS, ending in -aram: «visitaram».
exercises.givenAnswer: Sim, visitámos o museu de arte ontem.
acceptedAnswers: Visitaram o museu ontem?
Vocês visitaram o museu de arte ontem?
Visitaram o museu de arte ontem?

exercises.prompt: Manuel answers: «Decidi viajar para os Açores.» Ask him (informal) what he decided for the holidays.
exercises.explanation: The tu PPS of -ir verbs ends in -iste: «decidiste».
acceptedAnswers: O que é que decidiste para as férias?
O que decidiste fazer nas férias?
O que é que decidiste fazer nas férias?

exercises.prompt: Your flatmate answers: «Sim, limpei a cozinha e a sala.» Ask him (informal) whether he cleaned the house today.
exercises.explanation: A yes/no question keeps statement order; the tu PPS of -ar verbs ends in -aste: «limpaste».
exercises.givenAnswer: Sim, limpei a cozinha e a sala.
acceptedAnswers: Tu limpaste a casa hoje?

exercises.prompt: Rita answers: «Bebi dois litros de água durante a corrida.» Ask her (informal) how much water she drank during the race.
exercises.explanation: «Água» is feminine, so «Quanta água…?»; the tu PPS of -er verbs ends in -este: «bebeste».
exercises.givenAnswer: Bebi dois litros de água durante a corrida.
acceptedAnswers: Quanta água é que bebeste na corrida?
Quanta água bebeste durante a corrida?
Quanta água é que bebeste durante a corrida?

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: The 1st-person PPS of regular -ar verbs ends in -ei: «comprei», not present «compro».

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: The 3rd-person singular PPS of regular -er verbs ends in -eu: «comeu», not «comou».

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: The 2nd-person (tu) PPS of regular -ar verbs ends in -aste: «falaste», not «falou».

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: The 3rd-person PPS of regular -ir verbs ends in -iu: «partiu», not «parti».

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: The past time expression for last week uses the feminine adjective «passada»: «na semana passada».

exercises.prompt: Answer about yourself.
exercises.explanation: State what you bought yesterday using «Ontem comprei …».
exercises.question: O que compraste ontem?
exercises.sampleAnswer: Ontem comprei pão e café no supermercado.

exercises.prompt: Answer about yourself.
exercises.explanation: State what you ate for dinner yesterday using «Comi …» (eu form of «comer» in the PPS).
exercises.question: O que comeste ao jantar ontem à noite?
exercises.sampleAnswer: Comi peixe grelhado com legumes e arroz.

exercises.prompt: Answer about yourself.
exercises.explanation: State which city or monument you visited last year using «No ano passado visitei …».
exercises.question: Que cidade ou monumento visitaste no ano passado?
exercises.sampleAnswer: No ano passado visitei o castelo de Sintra.
